summary: At exact candidate commit f2422973285f9887a12aaa110cb0ce0fefff1d6e, the local deep_gemm import fixes the reproduced disabled-JIT NameError in the real entrypoint source. Candidate and independent tests verify non-empty forwarding, the empty-input fast path, and the missing-dependency boundary. This is a narrow source fix plus regression coverage.

tests.what_was_measured: The real base entrypoint with ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=false raised NameError on a non-empty call despite an importable deep_gemm substitute. Evidence: reports/j-cc0f8bebdf1c/raw/base-independent-contract.log
All three candidate regression cases passed when executed against the exact candidate checkout. Evidence: reports/j-cc0f8bebdf1c/raw/candidate-regression.log

An independent harness passed non-empty dependency import and exact forwarding, empty-input no-import behavior, and missing-dependency ImportError behavior. Evidence: reports/j-cc0f8bebdf1c/raw/candidate-independent-contract.log
Pytest collected and passed all three focused tests. Evidence: reports/j-cc0f8bebdf1c/raw/candidate-pytest.log
Both changed Python files compiled successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned GPU is AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 on ROCm 7.2. DeepSeek-V4 disables this DeepGEMM path on HIP, the environment has no deep_gemm package, and no CUDA H100/SM90 execution was possible. See reports/j-cc0f8bebdf1c/raw/environment.log

remaining_limitations: No CUDA H100/SM90 was available, so the actual DeepGEMM TF32 kernel was not launched or numerically validated.
DeepSeek-V4 weights were unavailable, so no full-model forward or HTTP serving reproduction was performed.
The prepared environment had no deep_gemm package; import behavior and forwarding were validated with a deterministic module substitute against the real entrypoint source.
A pre-commit attempt initialized hook environments but did not complete hook execution, so no pre-commit result is claimed.
